correctness.rationale: The projector-word contraction argument proves existence, uniqueness and finite fourth moments for every finite normalized spanning row family with strictly positive iid selection weights. A finite centered Gaussian mixture can equal a single Gaussian only if every updated covariance agrees; this forces each row to be a covariance eigenvector with its noise variance as eigenvalue. Orthogonal eigenspace geometry is equivalent to constancy along the nonorthogonality-graph components; the common covariance constructively proves sufficiency. Conditional Gaussianity given index history proves the nonnegative fourth-cumulant identity and strictness when compatibility fails. Exact rational checks in verify.py reproduce the overdetermined three-row example, covariance, nonzero cumulant, and independent two-row invariance cases. The proof uses no unverified finite-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns Gaussian versus genuinely non-Gaussian invariant distributions of fresh-noise randomized oblique row projections, with an exact all-row nonorthogonality-graph compatibility criterion and a positive-kurtosis witness. Inspected Kaczmarz sources establish convergence/error bounds or noiseless second-moment formulas, not an invariant-law Gaussianity classification. Switching-system work develops covariance enclosures rather than this exact graph criterion. The discrete Gibbs results supply an important analogous two-coordinate mixture statement; the distinct overcomplete arbitrary-row geometry and its Gaussianity equivalence do not follow from their stated discrete-coordinate conclusions. Similar general random affine iteration theory may still contain an equivalent formulation; this is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Gaussian stationary laws of general random affine recursions and incompatible Gibbs updates are broad areas; a source containing an equivalent all-row projector statement may remain undiscovered.
Chen–Ip covers the two-coordinate mixture aspect; that subcase is illustration rather than the asserted original contribution.
The manuscript should receive independent subject-expert novelty and proof assessment before any public attribution of priority.

value.rationale: Fresh noisy row observations are natural in repeated sensing and randomized linear-system solvers. Knowing a steady-state covariance does not settle Gaussian validity of confidence bands. This theorem gives a complete, easily testable all-dimension graph condition for Gaussianity, and otherwise proves positive directional excess kurtosis. The heterogeneous, overdetermined three-row example has an exact non-Gaussian cumulant. It isolates a structural design constraint rather than a routine parameter substitution or a tiny finite numerical improvement.
